sourcedFrom: FN FIVE-SEVEN® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2204-FN Five-seveN Mk3-OM 66-101364 (2021)
cleanIntro: The Five-seveN comes apart without a rotating takedown lever and without pressing the trigger: push the slide back a quarter of an inch, hold the takedown lever fully rearward, let the slide come forward and it lifts off the frame. This is FN's current book, written for the MRD version, and it opens by telling you how to check that it is describing your pistol.

steps.title: Read the barrel marking — this book is written for the MRD
steps.action: Look at the right side of the pistol and at the rear right end of the barrel through the ejection port, and find the caliber inscription. It should read cal. 5.7x28. Then compare the pistol against the illustrations in this manual.
steps.prose: FN states plainly that this edition was written exclusively for the FN Five-seveN MRD, and gives you two tests for whether it applies: the barrel inscription and whether the pistol looks like the drawings. Earlier Five-seveN pistols have their own FN manuals — the takedown manoeuvre is the same in the May 2020 book, but the optics mounting system and the parts around it are not. If the inscription or the appearance is different, get the book FN wrote for your pistol before going further.
steps.quote: This manual has been written exclusively for the FN Five‑seveN ® MRD pistols.
steps.cite: FN FIVE-SEVEN® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2204-FN Five-seveN Mk3-OM 66-101364 — Foreword / new gun owner's record, p.4
steps.warn: FN's instruction where it does not match: contact the FN Service Center or your departmental armorer to obtain the Owner's Manual that has been written specifically for your pistol.

steps.title: Safety to safe — no red marks showing
steps.action: Point the pistol in a safe direction and set the ambidextrous manual safety to the safe position. Confirm it by looking: when the safety is on, the red marks are not visible.
steps.prose: The Five-seveN's manual safety lever sits above the trigger on both sides of the frame, so it is reachable with either hand, and it is the first move in FN's own safety-check routine that every other procedure in the book refers back to. This pistol has an internal hammer you cannot see or feel, which is exactly why the visual red-mark check earns its place — there is no cocked spur to read. Get in the habit of confirming by the marks and not by the click.
steps.caution: Never try to decock the cocked hammer of a loaded FN Five-seveN MRD pistol — FN prints that as a standing warning at the head of the safety checks.
steps.quote: When the manual safety is at the “safe” position, the red marks are NOT visible.
steps.cite: FN FIVE-SEVEN® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2204-FN Five-seveN Mk3-OM 66-101364 — §4.1 Safety checks, p.27

steps.title: Magazine catch, magazine out
steps.action: Press the magazine catch and let the magazine eject. If it does not come out, pull on the bottom plate of the magazine.
steps.prose: The Five-seveN's 5.7x28 magazine is a long, slim column of small bottlenecked cartridges and its follower spring is stiff for its size, so a dirty magazine well can hold it in. Take it right out of the pistol and put it aside — this pistol has a magazine disconnect, so a partly seated magazine changes whether the trigger will do anything at all, which is a bad thing to be uncertain about mid-strip.
steps.aside: FN's note on the disconnect: the FN Five-seveN MRD pistol contains a magazine disconnect designed to prevent the pistol from being fired if the magazine has been removed.
steps.quote: Press the magazine catch to eject the magazine.
steps.cite: FN FIVE-SEVEN® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2204-FN Five-seveN Mk3-OM 66-101364 — §4.1 Safety checks, p.27

steps.title: Rack the chamber empty
steps.action: Pull the slide completely rearward and release it, ejecting any round from the chamber. If a round comes out, recover it, clean it and store it. If the slide is already locked back from the last shot, ease it forward first.
steps.prose: The Five-seveN's slide is light and its return spring is brisk, so let it go rather than riding it — a slow release is how a 5.7 round gets pushed part way back into the chamber instead of thrown clear. The cartridge indicator on this pistol protrudes when there is a round in the chamber, which is a useful confirmation of loaded and not a way to establish empty. That is what the next step is for.
steps.quote: Pull the slide completely rearward and then release it to eject any remaining round from the chamber.
steps.cite: FN FIVE-SEVEN® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2204-FN Five-seveN Mk3-OM 66-101364 — §4.1 Safety checks, p.27

steps.title: Look into the chamber through the ejection port, twice
steps.action: Pull the slide completely rearward and hold it there. Look through the ejection port into the chamber and confirm there is no round in it. Release the slide, then check the chamber a second time.
steps.prose: FN asks for the check and then asks for it again, which on a 5.7x28 pistol is not fussiness — the cartridge is small, the chamber is small, and a bottlenecked case sitting in shadow at the back of the port is easy to look straight past. If a round is in there and will not eject on a second rack, FN's instruction is to stop and consult the Service Center or your armorer rather than working at it. Empty the magazine too, one round at a time from the lips.
steps.quote: Double-check the chamber of the pistol to ensure that it is empty.
steps.cite: FN FIVE-SEVEN® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2204-FN Five-seveN Mk3-OM 66-101364 — §4.1 Safety checks, p.27

steps.title: For the strip only: no empty magazine, and leave the hammer cocked
steps.action: Run FN's safety checks as above, but with two deliberate omissions for disassembly: do not put an empty magazine back into the pistol, and do not decock the hammer.
steps.prose: Everywhere else in this book the safety checks end with an empty magazine inserted and the hammer decocked; for takedown FN suspends both, and the reason is mechanical. The internal hammer has to stay cocked for the slide assembly to come off and to go back on — FN repeats the same condition in the reassembly note — and the magazine disconnect means a magazine in the well changes what the fire control does. Get this wrong and the slide simply will not lift off the frame.
steps.quote: During the safety checks, DO NOT insert an empty magazine into the pistol and DO NOT decock the hammer.
steps.cite: FN FIVE-SEVEN® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2204-FN Five-seveN Mk3-OM 66-101364 — §6.1.1 Disassembling the pistol, p.41

steps.title: Slide back a quarter inch, takedown lever fully rearward
steps.action: Hold the pistol in your right hand. With the palm of your left hand push the slide about 0.25" rearward and hold it there. At the same time, with your left thumb, push the takedown lever completely rearward and hold that too.
steps.prose: This is the whole trick of the Five-seveN and it is two hands doing two things at once — a quarter of an inch of slide travel lines up the lever's clearance cut, and the lever has to go all the way back, not most of the way. Too much slide travel is as wrong as too little: push it back an inch and the cut moves past the lever. Palm flat on the rear of the slide gives you the control that fingertips do not.
steps.aside: FN's second half of the same movement: At the same time, and using the left thumb, push the takedown lever completely rearward and hold it in that position.
steps.quote: With the palm of the left hand, push the slide approximately 0.25” rearward and hold it in that position.
steps.cite: FN FIVE-SEVEN® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2204-FN Five-seveN Mk3-OM 66-101364 — §6.1.1 Disassembling the pistol, p.41

steps.title: Let the slide run forward with the lever held back
steps.action: Keeping the takedown lever pushed fully rearward, release the slide and let it move back forward.
steps.prose: The slide travelling forward against the held lever is what disengages the assembly — nothing is being forced, and if you find yourself pushing, the lever was not all the way back. Keep your thumb on the lever until the slide has finished its travel. There is no trigger press anywhere in this procedure, which is one of the real differences between the Five-seveN and the striker-fired FN pistols.
steps.quote: Release the slide so that it moves back forwards.
steps.cite: FN FIVE-SEVEN® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2204-FN Five-seveN Mk3-OM 66-101364 — §6.1.1 Disassembling the pistol, p.41

steps.title: Push the rear of the slide forward, then lift the assembly off
steps.action: With your right thumb, push forward on the rear end of the slide to disengage the complete slide assembly from the frame, then lift the assembly up and off.
steps.prose: It comes away as one piece — slide, barrel and return spring together — and the disengaging push is a short forward nudge at the back, not a heave. If the assembly will not lift, the usual causes are the hammer having been decocked or the takedown lever not having been held fully back through the previous step; reset and start the sequence again rather than prying at the rails. Set the frame down with the magazine well up.
steps.quote: With the right thumb, push forward on the rear end of the slide to disengage the complete slide assembly from the frame.
steps.cite: FN FIVE-SEVEN® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2204-FN Five-seveN Mk3-OM 66-101364 — §6.1.1 Disassembling the pistol, p.41

steps.title: Barrel out of the slide, rear end first
steps.action: Hold the slide assembly upside down, disengage the rear end of the barrel from the slide, then take the barrel out.
steps.prose: The Five-seveN is a delayed-blowback pistol, so the barrel is not a tilting, locking barrel like the 509's — it disengages at the rear and comes straight out with the return spring relaxing as it goes. Work it upside down as FN says, so the spring stays captured against the slide rather than jumping at you. That is the strip complete: frame, slide, barrel.
steps.quote: With the slide assembly held upside down, disengage the rear end of the barrel.
steps.cite: FN FIVE-SEVEN® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2204-FN Five-seveN Mk3-OM 66-101364 — §6.1.1 Disassembling the pistol, p.42

steps.title: Only the ammunition FN lists goes back in this pistol
steps.action: Before this Five-seveN is loaded again, check what you are feeding it. FN restricts it to new factory-manufactured 5.7x28mm supersonic ammunition and then names the specific loads by designation in the same section.
steps.prose: This is unusually tight even by manufacturer standards, and it exists because a delayed-blowback action is timed to a narrow pressure and impulse window — subsonic or unlisted 5.7x28 can leave the action unlocking at the wrong moment. The magazine is bound the same way: FN says it is unique to this pistol and that neither it nor any other magazine should be swapped between pistols. Keep the ammunition and the magazine within what the book names and the pistol behaves as its cleaning schedule assumes.
steps.quote: The FN Five‑seveN® MRD pistol must only be used with the following new factory manufactured 5.7x28mm supersonic ammunition:
steps.cite: FN FIVE-SEVEN® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2204-FN Five-seveN Mk3-OM 66-101364 — §2.3 Magazines and ammunition, p.24
steps.warn: FN's magazine restriction, from the same section: This magazine is unique for the FN Five-seveN MRD pistol and should not be used in other pistols and no other magazines should be used in your FN Five-seveN MRD pistol.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Three groups: frame, slide with its return spring, and barrel. FN calls that enough for a thorough clean and puts anything beyond it in the hands of a qualified armorer or the FN Service Center.
steps.prose: From here the bore and chamber, the breech face, the extractor, the upper part of the frame and the slide's guide grooves are all reachable — which is the full list of places FN's cleaning section sends you. Clean after every use, or every 500 rounds under intensive shooting. The magazine strip and the optic mounting are the deeper procedures this book publishes, and they sit behind Deep Clean.
steps.quote: CAUTION This level of disassembly is sufficient to perform thorough cleaning. Further disassembly should only be carried out by a qualified armorer or by the FN Service Center.
steps.cite: FN FIVE-SEVEN® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2204-FN Five-seveN Mk3-OM 66-101364 — §6.1.1 Disassembling the pistol, closing caution, p.43

deepSteps.title: Magazine apart — bottom plate against something soft
deepSteps.action: Empty the magazine first. Hold the rear end of the magazine bottom plate against a solid but soft surface and press down on the magazine to disengage the plate. Keeping control of the spring load, slide the bottom plate off the body, release the spring pressure carefully, and take out the follower and the follower spring.
deepSteps.prose: The soft surface is not politeness — FN says a hard one will damage the bottom plate, and a bent plate on a 5.7 magazine is a feeding problem you will chase for weeks. The plate is directly under the force of the follower spring, so it comes off sideways with your hand over it, never straight off. Only strip it when the magazine is visibly soiled; FN says magazine disassembly for cleaning is needed only in that case.
deepSteps.quote: While holding the rear end of the magazine bottom plate against a solid but soft surface, press down on the magazine to disengage the bottom plate.
deepSteps.cite: FN FIVE-SEVEN® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2204-FN Five-seveN Mk3-OM 66-101364 — §6.2.1 Disassembling and reassembling the 20-round magazine, p.45
deepSteps.warn: Using a hard surface may damage the magazine bottom plate.

deepSteps.title: Magazine back together, plate locked
deepSteps.action: Clean every part, then rebuild in reverse: follower and follower spring correctly oriented, spring compressed and held flush with the edge of the magazine body, bottom plate slid back into position, and confirm the plate has locked.
deepSteps.prose: The plate will only go back on with the spring compressed level with the body edge, so if it is fighting you the spring is proud somewhere and you are about to bend the plate. Lightly oil the follower spring with a lubricated patch, wipe the excess off, and leave the inside of the magazine dry — oil inside a magazine collects the grit that stops the follower. Check the plate is genuinely locked before the magazine goes near the pistol.
deepSteps.quote: The magazine bottom plate can only be slid back into position when the follower spring is compressed and held flush with the edge of the magazine body.
deepSteps.cite: FN FIVE-SEVEN® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2204-FN Five-seveN Mk3-OM 66-101364 — §6.2.1 Reassembly, p.45

deepSteps.title: Under the optic: dry screws, then threadlocker on the screws only
deepSteps.action: If you are cleaning the optic mount, run the safety checks, back the two securing screws out counterclockwise with the T10 Torx, remove the cover plate, and inspect and clean the mounting surface on top of the slide. Rebuild with all lubricant removed from the screws and their holes, then apply a medium-strength threadlocker to both screws and tighten clockwise, respecting the cure time.
deepSteps.prose: Note that the Five-seveN's mounting system takes the opposite instruction to FN's low-profile system on the 509 — here a medium-strength threadlocker such as Loctite Blue 242 is specified, and lubricant in the threads is what must be removed. The interface and screw set have to match the optic, which is what the mounting-system chart in this section is for. Let the threadlocker cure before shooting, or the first string will undo the work.
deepSteps.quote: Add a medium-strength threadlocker, such as Loctite Blue 242® to both securing screws and tighten clockwise with the provided T10 Torx wrench.
deepSteps.cite: FN FIVE-SEVEN® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2204-FN Five-seveN Mk3-OM 66-101364 — §5.1 Installing an optic, p.38

deepSteps.title: Lubricate the named points — and never the breech face
deepSteps.action: After cleaning, put one drop of lubricant on the outer surface of the barrel, the return spring, the inside of the slide — especially the grooves for the guide slides and the part of the slide bottom that contacts the hammer — the frame's guide slides, and the hammer where it meets the slide. Put none on the breech face.
deepSteps.prose: That list is short and specific and it is worth following literally, because on a delayed-blowback pistol the slide-to-frame guide grooves are doing the timing work. Oil on the breech face is FN's explicit exception: it migrates into the chamber and onto primers, and there is nothing there that needs it. Excess lubricant anywhere on this pistol collects dirt, grit and powder residue, which is the failure mode FN names in the same section.
deepSteps.quote: Never apply lubricant to the breech face.
deepSteps.cite: FN FIVE-SEVEN® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2204-FN Five-seveN Mk3-OM 66-101364 — §6.4.2 Cleaning and lubrication after firing, p.51

deepSteps.title: The round count that is not a cleaning interval
deepSteps.action: Log the rounds through this pistol. Separately from cleaning, FN wants it inspected every 2000 rounds or once a year, whichever comes first, because wear and corrosion are not always visible from outside.
deepSteps.prose: It is easy to read the 500-round cleaning figure as the only number that matters; this is the other one, and it is an inspection rather than a clean. A Five-seveN that has been cleaned faithfully can still be wearing internally where nothing you can reach at field-strip level will show it. For departmental pistols FN puts this on the armorer's annual schedule; for a private owner it is a note in the log and a trip to the Service Center.
deepSteps.quote: The pistol should be checked every 2000 rounds and/or once a year because damage, wear, or corrosion are not always visible from the outside.
deepSteps.cite: FN FIVE-SEVEN® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2204-FN Five-seveN Mk3-OM 66-101364 — §6.5 Additional care, p.51

cleaning.name: BARREL — BORE AND CHAMBER
tasks: Brush or spray solvent into the bore and chamber and let it work for a few minutes
Rod and patches back and forth until the last patch comes out clean — the 5.7's small bore fouls quickly and a single pass will lie to you
Then a patch moistened with lubricant through the bore to protect it until next use
Before shooting, wipe the inside of the barrel dry again and check it for obstructions with the slide held back

cleaning.name: SLIDE, EXTRACTOR & FRAME
tasks: Cleaning brushes and solvent on the slide, the extractor and the upper part of the frame, where powder and primer residue settles
Soft cloth or patch, dipped in solvent if needed, through the magazine housing of the frame
Check the stripped parts for wear or damage while they are apart; anything doubtful goes to the FN Service Center or your armorer
Clean the outside afterwards to remove dirt, fingerprint residue and excess lubricant

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION & INTERVAL
tasks: One drop each: outer surface of the barrel, the return spring, inside the slide including the guide-slide grooves and the hammer contact area, the frame guide slides, and the hammer itself
Clean and lubricate after every use, or after 500 rounds in intensive shooting; dirty ammunition brings that forward
Avoid prolonged exposure to hydrocarbons, trichlorethylene and ammonia — FN warns these can damage the pistol
Magazine cleaning only when it is visibly soiled: lubricate the follower spring lightly, wipe the excess, leave the inside dry

reassembly: Check every component is clean, then insert the muzzle of the barrel into the barrel opening at the front of the slide.
Push the barrel slightly forward against the return spring and fit its rear end into position in the slide.
Before the assembly goes on: stripping lever at the rear position, no magazine in the frame, hammer cocked — all three, or it will not seat.

Hold the slide assembly parallel above the frame, align its rear end with the front of the frame's rear guide slides, lower it on and move it slightly rearward so the front and rear guide slides enter the grooves.
Confirm the slide assembly has engaged the frame, move it fully rearward, and check it runs back and forth smoothly.
fncheck: With the pistol empty: the slide should move back and forth smoothly on the frame guide slides with no binding; the takedown lever should return to and stay at its forward position; the ambidextrous manual safety should move between fire and safe from either side, with the red marks hidden when it is on safe; an empty magazine should seat and drop free on the catch; and with no magazine in the well the magazine disconnect should prevent the pistol firing — bearing in mind FN's standing warning never to attempt to decock a cocked hammer on a loaded Five-seveN.
